name: security-sudo-command-policy-review
intent: sudo policy matching, delegated arguments and executable provenance
artifacts: Effective sudoers/includes, runas settings, allowed arguments/environment and script/binary ownership.
trace: Resolve the exact matched command and who controls its executable, parameters, configuration and working-directory dependencies.
experiment: Use an isolated local policy fixture or inert argv-recording stub under owned identities; do not execute privileged escape payloads.
disproof: A sudo entry is intentional delegation; demonstrate unintended authority beyond its actual command and argument contract.
repair: Constrain the delegated operation and mutable inputs, verifying authorized commands and rejected argument/environment changes.
branch_decisions: Apply the installed sudo version matching rules to the exact executable and arguments before analyzing helper behavior. Wildcards, regular expressions, environment controls and writable executable/parent paths have distinct implications. A matcher granting a command is expected when policy intends it; the defect is an unauthorized semantic effect reachable through that permitted helper.
operational_method: Retain installed sudo version, effective includes/order/tags, RunAs identity, canonical executable and how that version matches the command argument string. Resolve wildcard versus supported regex semantics rather than assuming shell argv matching. Inspect writable executable/parent paths, permitted environment and helper dependencies. A local argv recorder proves arguments only; validate the actual sudo matching decision from supplied policy/output or an isolated policy fixture before attributing the helper semantic effect.
